$comment: The sidecar's TELEMETRY keys, recorded. Read by internal/ai's wire test.
It exists because of a bug that made the POC detect nothing at all and say so
in a way that looked deliberate: the sidecar began sending `input_w` and
`input_h`, the Go sidecar client declares `DisallowUnknownFields`, and so
EVERY reply was refused. 169 of 169 frames came back `cannot_tell` with the
reason buried in a fault row. Nothing was red. The tests were green. The
report said `cannot_tell`, which is a designed state, so it read as the
A strict decoder is correct and is not negotiable — it is what caught this. So
the guard is not 'be lenient'; it is that the two sides are PINNED against each
other, and adding a field on one side without the other becomes a test failure
instead of a whole silent run.
HOW IT IS KEPT TRUE, both directions:
- pyworker/test_wire.py builds a real telemetry dict and asserts its key set
equals this file, so a field added on the Python side fails there;
- internal/ai/wire_test.go decodes a payload with every key from this file
using the same strict decoder production uses, so a field missing on the Go
